options.ratio: 1 cup maida → 1 cup atta plus 2 tbsp extra water. Rest the dough 20 minutes longer.
options.taste_and_texture: Denser, less stretchy, tears rather than folds. Bad for anything that needs to be laminated or paper-thin; fine for everyday breads.
options.nutritional_rationale: Fibre up, and the germ carries fat-soluble vitamins the mill removes.

options.swap: Pearl millet (bajra), finger millet (ragi) or sorghum (jowar)
options.ratio: Start at 1 cup maida → 3/4 cup millet flour plus 1/4 cup whole wheat. Pure millet flour has no gluten and will not roll without practice.
options.taste_and_texture: Earthy, sometimes bitter with bajra. Cracks at the edge when rolled. Honestly harder to work with, this is a swap that costs you something.
options.nutritional_rationale: Ragi is notably higher in calcium; bajra and jowar higher in iron and fibre than refined wheat. Lower glycaemic load.

where_it_went: Roller mills separated bran and germ cheaply, giving flour a long shelf life; post-Independence procurement centred on wheat, and millets left the supply chain.
